title: Privacy.
summary: Privacy information for An AUsome Life.
search: Site information · updated October 3, 2026Privacy.Useful tools, with clear choices about your words and pictures.The current websiteAn AUsome Life is a static website hosted through GitHub Pages. We do not operate visitor accounts, checkout, comments, a public upload gallery or an on-site contact form. We do not currently use our own advertising cookies or behavioral analytics.GitHub states that GitHub Pages logs visitors’ IP addresses for security. Read GitHub’s explanation. Page and image requests still reach the hosting provider even when a tool processes your input locally.Picture cards & visit plansWords typed into the picture-card and visit-plan editors and photos selected from your device are processed in the open browser tab. These tools do not send that text or those photos to us or an image provider, and they do not save your edited plan on our server. Save or print before closing or reloading.A saved PNG or PDF becomes a file on the device or in the destination you choose. The website cannot delete those copies. On a shared device, close the editing tab and consider where downloaded files and print jobs are kept.Public event or place links may prefill a plan using information in the link. URLs can appear in browser history and hosting logs, so do not put private names, care information or other sensitive details into a shared URL.Image prompts & future generationThe image-prompt helper prepares text for you to copy. “Copy prompt & open ChatGPT” places that text on your clipboard and opens ChatGPT; it does not submit your prompt. If you paste it into a separate AI service, that service’s privacy and retention terms apply. Use a general description when a person’s name, diagnosis or private address is unnecessary.This site does not currently research or generate a new image live for a visitor. Before a live service is introduced, we will explain what is sent, which providers process it, how long it is retained and what choices you have. Your local photos will not be silently sent as references.External services & contactOpening a map, retailer, social account or video preview takes you to another service. An activated video player may load content from that provider. Those services have their own privacy practices. Read-aloud uses voices made available by your browser or operating system, which may rely on a separate service.If you email us, the email providers process the information you choose to send. We use it to respond and address the matter raised. Please leave private care records and unnecessary identifying details out of an initial message.Questions or privacy concerns? Contact the editor. This page will be updated when the site’s data practices change.

In everyday company, start by speaking to the person you are with. Make room for the communication methods they use and the time they need. Their usual support can be part of the conversation without the conversation passing them by. Ask about an actual preference, such as where to sit or what to do next.Keep familiar communication tools available and ask before touching them.Avoid piling several questions together or answering immediately on the person's behalf.Use a tone that respects their age, including when the words need to be straightforward. A person can need extensive help throughout the day and still have very clear views about where to sit, what to wear, when to leave and whether your idea is any good. Their preferences belong in the plan.Read our detailed guide to multimodal communication, AAC, access methods and communication-partner support → Plan the good part first.+ A swim, a familiar lunch, time outside or a favorite shop can be enough for a day out. Choose the part that matters most, then check the practical details that make it possible: arrival, waiting, food, bathrooms, breaks and the way home. Describe the plan in a familiar format. Actual photographs, objects, words or the person's established communication system may be useful. Include what comes afterward and how a change of plan will be explained. Keep a shorter version ready. Think through what happens if the visit is brief. Can you leave and return? Is there somewhere comfortable to pause? Can one family member finish an activity while another leaves with their support person? Agree on the practical arrangements before everyone is tired. Bring the everyday supplies and communication equipment the person ordinarily uses, and follow their existing support plans. Where possible, distribute the packing, transport and checking among the people available to help. Afterward, ask what worked and notice what the person chose to return to. Repeating a familiar pleasure is a perfectly good plan. A family outing does not become morally superior because it lasted six hours. Dignity lives in the small decisions.+ Privacy matters at home, with friends and online. A difficult moment, personal care or an intimate detail can stay private. Before sharing a story or photograph, consider whose experience it is, what the person has communicated about it, and whether the detail needs to be public at all. Leave it out when permission is unclear. A useful handover can be brief. For an activity host or someone helping with the day, share the practical information they need: how the person communicates, what support helps them take part, how to offer a break and whom to contact if plans change. Keep private care information with the appropriate people through a suitable private channel. A simple starting point is: “Please speak directly to them and allow time to respond. They communicate using [method]. For this activity, [specific support] helps. If they want to pause, [familiar signal or arrangement].” Adapt it to the person and the setting. The useful questions remain ordinary ones. Did they have a say? Could they join in with the help they needed? Was there room to stop? Were their private moments protected? Those details make everyday life more considerate for the person at its center. Planning suggestions to adapt to the person and the day.
